verdict.paragraph: JASA scores 61 out of 100, a visible gap from a strong result but closer than most manufacturers at this stage. The fixes are specific and contained. Ulma Packaging sits just ahead at 66, and it pulls that lead almost entirely from trade show and print materials, which is exactly where JASA should focus first. Sharpen that category and the gap closes fast.

firstFix.why: Trade show and print is where fresh produce buyers make shortlist decisions. A buyer who visits the GreenTech booth and asks for a brochure on a machine other than the 400X leaves empty-handed. Ulma Packaging pulls its lead over JASA almost entirely from this category. Closing that gap does not require a full rebrand, just materials that match the quality already visible on the website.
firstFix.inPractice: Start by building a one-page data sheet for each core machine in the range, using the same green and red palette and photography already on the site. Host all sheets in a single downloadable library on the website. Before GreenTech 2026, produce a printed folder that holds those sheets so booth visitors leave with something tangible. That alone addresses the two biggest gaps: missing product coverage and no visible print-to-web consistency.
